rows.latBasis: Median per request · 1 in flight · run · runs 346 · 1 questions/request

rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.tent: Knowledgator's released GLiClass v4 Edge (knowledgator/gliclass-v4-edge at 885af1a), a zero-shot classifier fine-tuned from DeBERTa-v3-large (supervised training, reinforcement learning, then a calibrator). It ran on our hardware (one DGX Spark), one request at a time, through our HTTP server (servers/gliclass_server.py) with that mapping and gliclass 0.1.22, in BF16, text only; a request over 16,384 tokens (the card's limit) is refused, never cut. Its card lists English only.

rows.name: SubQ Snap 1.1
rows.latBasis: Median per request · 1 in flight · run · runs 346
rows.method: Five option Turkish exam questions, scored against the published answer key. · SubQ Decisions API (public preview)
rows.costBasis: api · at list prices
rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.tent: Knowledgator's released GLiClass v4 Edge (knowledgator/gliclass-v4-edge at 885af1a), a zero-shot classifier fine-tuned from DeBERTa-v3-large (supervised training, reinforcement learning, then a calibrator). Its card serves it as a library pipeline (gliclass) and maps a decision request onto it: the passage is the text, the instructions the prompt, each option a label, and a softmax over the calibrated label scores. It ran on our hardware (one DGX Spark), one request at a time, through our HTTP server (servers/gliclass_server.py) with that mapping and gliclass 0.1.22, in BF16, text only; a request over 16,384 tokens (the card's limit) is refused, never cut. Its card lists English only.

rows.name: Strands Decider 2B
rows.ref: tool-choice:Strands Decider 2B|our GPU: maker decision server
rows.method: Mean of the five Tools & Automation benchmarks of the Decision Index kit (apolinario/decision-index@25c6ec7 (MIT), Tools & Automation area, edition 0.3 scorer), one request at a time
rows.limit: Its own server (strands_decider serve, maker default, as for its Logic & Math run) truncates a prompt longer than its 4,096-token window instead of refusing it (--strict-window is off by default). By the kit's token count 1,185 of 6,627 requests exceed that window (ToolRet 672 of 685, API-Bank 508 of 508, BFCL 2, When2Call 3); they were answered from a truncated prompt. Other servers refuse over-limit requests, which count as unsupported.
